scope: Pure monotonic boundary and callback gateway only, under trusted adapter assumptions. No placement or host integration.
behavior: Keeps one original origin, including zero, and checked monotonic samples with safe integer arithmetic. Normal reserve refusal remains separate from fatal hard deadline and captured operation overrun.
Checks both callback resolution and rejection, retains raw settled outcome before post-check, and latches the first private fatal identity.

R2 rechecks fatal after then-property inspection. A nonnative then body cannot begin after that fatal. An already-running trusted native Promise still reaches actual settlement before the gateway rejects.
No new callback or clock sample follows a latched fatal; cached snapshot and outcome remain readable. Concurrent admission is refused.

revisionHistory.finding: A then getter could latch fatal and return a function that r1 still invoked. The original failed evidence is preserved; restoration of the flaw is detected by the r2 mutation control.

limitations: Clock, phase and caps are trusted inputs, not authority. Native Promise subclass/species behavior also relies on trusted adapters. This is not an arbitrary-object sandbox.
Nonnative thenables after fatal are not assimilated and have no settlement guarantee. Nonsettling callbacks have no containment or cancellation proof.
Raw outcome retention is not effect verification and does not imply performed:NO.
No placement, ledger, bridge, host, PostgreSQL, browser, SSH, actual limits, deployment or production wiring was tested.
The host wall-clock and catch-unwind paths remain unchanged; TF2 integration and later host gates are still required. PM-1 S1 is unchanged.
next: Implement the reviewed pure TF2 placement successor with private ledger-clock provenance and independent cutoff tests; preserve frozen sources and measured-approval gates.
